reviews.text: There's certainly a hidden gravity to the film, a low-key melancholy. But nonetheless Palm Spring is absolutely a comedy, albeit a dark one—ironically set in sunny paradise.
reviews.author: Brandon Stanwyck

reviews.text: This is one film I was desperate to see, and I am so glad I loved it as much as I thought I would.
reviews.author: Amy Smith

reviews.text: Instead the conceit is elevated, thanks to updated material and two stars who can effortlessly go from irreverent to goofy to swoon-worthy in the same scene.
reviews.author: Patricia Karounos

reviews.text: With a fast pace and a perfect balance of its tone, Palm Springs sets itself apart from the other movies of the genre, staying away from all of the cliches, formulas, and stereotypes associated with it. One of the best rom-coms I’ve ever seen.
reviews.author: Manuel São Bento

reviews.text: Palm Springs is the perfect package of sharp comedy and sci-fi intrigue.
reviews.author: Jennifer Bisset

reviews.text: Palm Springs is an absolutely winning comedy, and you won’t see a better one all year.
reviews.author: M.N. Miller

reviews.text: Palm Springs gives a fresh coat of paint to the oft-parodied plot of Groundhog Day with thought-provoking twists on that familiar formula.
reviews.author: Zoë Rose Bryant

reviews.text: “Palm Springs” is essentially a less attractive and less nuanced “Groundhog Day”.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: “Palm Springs” is the perfect balance of hilarious comedy and insightful writing, and it does what all the best films should do - it makes us reflect on our own existence.
reviews.author: Cody Dericks

reviews.text: Its the sweetness of the central relationship that makes Palm Springs one of the few times youll relish going to a destination wedding.
reviews.author: Victoria Luxford

reviews.text: Palm Springs eerily works as a metaphor for the growth and establishment of relationships and the feeling the current pandemic has created  living life in a constant loop.
reviews.author: David Gonzalez

reviews.text: With an incredibly smart screenplay and cast, it is a film that not only provides plenty of laughs, but also some legitimate heart and soul.
reviews.author: Carson Timar

reviews.text: If you can handle more repetition in the name of fun and entertainment there's actually a lot to be gained from the film's gentle dissection of human foibles and the meaningless nature of time.
reviews.author: Dorothy Woodend

reviews.text: What starts as a goofy, skit-like Groundhog Day morphs into a pleasant and interesting existential romance.
reviews.author: Lonita Cook

reviews.text: In theaters, this kind of brainy weirdo comedy nearly always underperforms. But in the arena of the streaming world, it breaks through and offers you a psychic daiquiri. Good enough.
reviews.author: Jason Shawhan

reviews.text: The chemistry between Samberg and Milioti shines through in one of the funniest, absurdly charming movies of 2020.
reviews.author: Emily Tannenbaum

reviews.text: The movie comes out of the gate with a speed and charm that's difficult to match. It's fittingly self-reflexive, though, that the movie's only real letdown comes after looping through so much fun.
reviews.author: Jesse Hassenger

reviews.text: By the time the end credits roll, Palm Springs has created its own sort of loop: you have seen it all before, and you will likely see it again.
reviews.author: Steven Warner

reviews.text: "Others films may have done [the time loop concept] better, but the emotional journey the characters go on is a little different here, and the time loop idea plays into that journey."
reviews.author: Jim Ross

reviews.text: Palm Springs covers the big topic of finding something to live for and the value of companionship, but with a unique goofiness mixed with unexpected poignancy. I
reviews.author: Amelia Harvey

reviews.text: For while it's certainly not original, it is funny, crowd-pleasing and nicely played out by its two leads, Andy Samberg and Cristin Milioti.
reviews.author: Matthew Bond

reviews.text: Fans of sci-fi, buddy movies, sitcoms and towering love stories alike can rejoice: Palm Springs finds the sweet spot in all of them, understanding love and pain as transcendental, fear and desire as lifeblood.
reviews.author: Ella Kemp

reviews.text: Play it again, Samberg.
reviews.author: Charlotte O'Sullivan

reviews.text: This meaty genre subversion brings out its perceptual metaphor of our generational angst and stasis -- and in turn manifests what it takes to better ourselves in a seemingly unworthy and emotionless world of existential dread.
reviews.author: Weiting Liu

reviews.text: This may just be the most perfect use of 90 minutes of screentime that we've seen in a long time, let alone the best use of a time loop/Groundhog Day narrative.
reviews.author: Charlotte Harrison

reviews.text: Surface similarities to Groundhog Day are relegated to background noise, thanks to the crisp writing and the nihilistic bite of the humour.
reviews.author: Wendy Ide

reviews.text: A philosophical comedy that is not afraid to aim the odd joke below the belt or, as resolution looms, to give in to sentimentality.
reviews.author: Donald Clarke

reviews.text: The boredom, the dread and the existential terror. It's all there. Only this time it's funny.
reviews.author: Kevin Maher

reviews.text: Max Barbakow's debut film, written by Andy Siara, offers a new way to look at a familiar format.
reviews.author: Clarisse Loughrey

reviews.text: Surprisingly, the film is able to tackle some pretty hefty existential issues, all the while offering up a genuinely heartening love story.
reviews.author: Linda Marric

reviews.text: Part comedy, part cautionary fable, Palm Springs lands its big ideas as lightly as its punchlines.
reviews.author: Robbie Collin

reviews.text: I'd like to watch it again.
reviews.author: Peter Bradshaw

reviews.text: A wonderful, witty and weird spin on an old favourite, which seems destined to become a classic itself.
reviews.author: Nick De Semlyen

reviews.text: A highly enjoyable movie - the kind that you could see yourself introducing your friends to, and going back to re-watch in a few months time.
reviews.author: Deirdre Molumby

reviews.text: The premise might be pure fantasy but it's a rom-com at heart.
reviews.author: Emma Simmonds

reviews.text: ...a unromantic, caustic rom-com which rolls over to reveal grown-up, idealistic sentiment, but only after pigging out in cheerfully anarchic style...
reviews.author: Eddie Harrison

reviews.text: The 'Groundhog Day' premise is becoming a subgenre unto itself, but 'Palm Springs,' in addition to being riotously funny, adds a warm and welcome layer of existential philosophy.
reviews.author: Witney Seibold

reviews.text: Palm Springs still stands out because it's so deeply interested in the beauty and difficulty of knowing and being known by someone.. . I don't believe Sarah denied Nyles consent in the traditional sense, but... it gets sticky.
reviews.author: Sarah Jae Leiber

reviews.text: It would be easy to dismiss Palm Springs as a Groundhog Day rip-off. It would also be myopic, misguided, and moronic.
reviews.author: Matt Brunson

reviews.text: The filmmakers use the hook of the time-loop to do some clever, creative things they could not do were this just some linear movie set at a Palm Springs wedding.
reviews.author: Mark Meszoros

reviews.text: A fun film that unintentionally speaks to the COVID era - anxiety, depression and that feeling that no matter what you do, you can't escape yourself. The good news is that, in this movie anyway, there's a cure for that.
reviews.author: Karen Gordon

reviews.text: It's a film you might want to watch more than once to catch everything, and you'll find it an enjoyable way to spend your time.
reviews.author: Jennie Kermode

reviews.text: Coming in at the ideal 90 minutes, Palm Springs gives you everything you could want out of this type of film. The characters are relatable, the situations are wild and tons of fun, and it exits stage left before overplaying its hand.
reviews.author: Alex Bentley

reviews.text: Palm Springs builds on the concept's legacy by using it to examine negotiations between two people instead of a path for self-betterment.
reviews.author: Esther Zuckerman

reviews.text: This movie is more than worth a watch - and one that I think will become timeless (no pun intended).
reviews.author: Tessa Smith

reviews.text: This breezy, irreverent, oddly violent and charming entry into this increasingly robust genre stands solidly on its own.
reviews.author: Lindsey Bahr

reviews.text: It tackles some profound topics amid the laughs, interrogating the sustainability of long-term relationships and exploring how a seemingly awful situation might be aided by a change in perspective.
reviews.author: Ben Pearson

reviews.text: Considering this movie is about the limitless potential of being immortal and living without consequence, it does fall into pretty familiar and tired arenas towards the end.
reviews.author: Simon Miraudo

reviews.text: The time loop rom-com is a slim genre, but Palm Springs is a worthy addition.
reviews.author: Richard Crouse

reviews.text: Watch [Palm Springs] when you're down and need to climb back up
reviews.author: Sean Fennessey

reviews.text: [A] quite exemplary romantic comedy. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Daniel de Partearroyo

reviews.text: Rom-com hijinks ensue, spring-break neons flood the desert oasis cinematography, drama emerges, and, ultimately, Conner O'Malley steals the show.
reviews.author: Luke Hicks

reviews.text: The cleverness of Max Barbakow's direction blended with the originality of Andy Siara's screenplay result in a fast-paced, extremely diverting 90 minutes.
reviews.author: Steve Crum

reviews.text: This is a complex story about love and emotional growth in a strange and seemingly hopeless situation which nonetheless is similar to the human condition we all share. As a time-loop romantic comedy, it ranks right up there with "Groundhog Day."
reviews.author: Robert Roten

reviews.text: In the time-honoured tradition of Adam Sandler, Jim Carrey, Chris Rock or Kristin Wiig, [Andy] Samberg here proves himself very capable of merging his comedic talents with something more dramatic and tragic.
reviews.author: Alex Hudson

reviews.text: [The introspective drama's] emotional and psychological revelations will always be undercut by comedy, but they're no less effective for it.
reviews.author: Jared Mobarak

reviews.text: You could revisit [this film] many times. It's also difficult to imagine a film that better encapsulates the loopy feeling of living through a pandemic, minus the fear. It's one of the best and brightest things to come out of this benighted year.
reviews.author: Chris Knight

reviews.text: Maybe Palm Springs should be the last time-loop movie. It certainly sends the genre out on a high.
reviews.author: Norman Wilner

reviews.text: A delicate mash-up of meet-cute and time looping tropes that works rather well, even though the film constantly feels like it's about to fall apart at any moment.
reviews.author: Andrew Parker

reviews.text: Despite of a promising start, Palm Springs runs out of inspiration, settling down in a thousand unremarkable 'wake ups' that lead to nowhere.
reviews.author: Filipe Freitas

reviews.text: As Nyles and Sarah adjust to a life where consequences no longer exist, the two performers make you believe that, actually, everything the two characters do matters.
reviews.author: Barry Hertz

reviews.text: Palm Springs is an audience-pleasing debut for Barbakow. With Samberg and Milioti stealing the show on and off the dancefloor, it is essentially Groundhog Day with piña coladas.
reviews.author: Katie Smith-Wong

reviews.text: All charm, heart and hilarity, Palm Springs is one of the year's best films.
reviews.author: Wenlei Ma

reviews.text: For a film about time loops, this is one you wouldn't mind watching over and over again.
reviews.author: Morris Yang

reviews.text: "Palm Springs" brings both levity and poignancy...by reminding us of the gift of presence.
reviews.author: Joel Mayward

reviews.text: Uses an excellent cast and a surprisingly thoughtful story to elevate the formula to another level-making it not only a welcome addition to the genre, but one of the best comedies to come out this year.
reviews.author: Katie Parker

reviews.text: As much as it tangles with life's essential meaninglessness, Palm Springs keeps walking back uncertainty with easy humour, dodging the abyss with charm.
reviews.author: Luke Goodsell

reviews.text: Samberg, a little more knowing and more of a jerk than usual, is perfect and Milioti brings a sublime blend of vulnerability, steel and unpredictability.
reviews.author: Brad Newsome

reviews.text: Palm Springs treats the idea as a jazz player might treat the chord changes of a standard - somewhere to poke around in and find new expression. I think Ramis might have been flattered.
reviews.author: Paul Byrnes

reviews.text: In a year when we've all felt like our daily lives have occasionally been stuck on repeat, Palm Springs is the perfect uplifting, sci-fi-infused comedy to help, at least temporarily, shake off that ennui and those pandemic blues.
reviews.author: James Croot

reviews.text: Seemingly enjoying the fact that it constantly tests the limits of its concept throughout its brisk 90 minute running time, Palm Springs is an earnest, heartfelt film that's both emotionally mature and comedically youthful.
reviews.author: Peter Gray

reviews.text: Sarah glows with a complex inner life, and the connection she makes with Nyles leads to outrageous capers and silliness in a truly enjoyable way.
reviews.author: Diane Pershing

reviews.text: An uplifting and optimistic piece of escapism that looks to the future after realising we can't dwell in the present forever... arguably the perfect film to watch in 2020.
reviews.author: Sol Harris

reviews.text: We all know Andy Samberg and Cristin Milioti's comedic skills. I loved the relationship of their characters. If we add the many references to films like Groundhog Day (1993) we will really enjoy the movie. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Alvaro Corujo

reviews.text: The chemistry between Samberg and Milioti makes the romance believable and endearing. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Emmanuel Báez

reviews.text: Samberg and Milioti are beautiful together and Palm Springs has the perfect midsummer vibe.
reviews.author: Brian Gill

reviews.text: A clever, very funny and effectively performed rom-com that runs rings around most other recent laffers.
reviews.author: Caffeinated Clint

reviews.text: The film is smart and funny. It knows how to show the human side of comedy, because in the end, no one laughs at something they don't identify with. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Victor Pineyro

reviews.text: J.K. Simmons is just crazy in this movie, and I love him in the film. He gets to do a lot with a relatively small role...
reviews.author: Korey Coleman

reviews.text: I was so pleasantly surprised, I really fell in love with this...find somebody and watch this again, it's fun and it's clever.
reviews.author: Martin Thomas

reviews.text: When Palm Springs leads with its rom-com aspects, the film starts to pick up steam, especially when the two engage in creative date ideas like our own current quarantine reality.
reviews.author: Ade Adeniji

reviews.text: I get a pleasant surprise watching 'Palm Springs', a romantic comedy that captures the paradox of time loops with wit, grace, and never-failing fun with the couple caught in the eternal return of love. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Yasser Medina

reviews.text: It offers a fresh take on the familiar rom-com genre thanks to its peculiar premise. Andy Samberg and Cristin Milioti are fantastic in this profound, hilarious and charming love story. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Rene Sanchez

reviews.text: Milioti is a wonder. She steals the movie from the ostensible star (Samberg) without taking anything from him.
reviews.author: Eleanor Ringel Cater

reviews.text: This is probably one of my favorite movies of 2020 so far. It's everything that i wanted it to be. I loved every second of it. I would watch it a million more times.
reviews.author: Steph Cozza

reviews.text: While its ties to Groundhog Day are apparent from the get-go, Palm Springs charms with a refreshing and clever spin on the format.
reviews.author: Michelle Jaworski

reviews.text: Even harder is pulling off a comedy with a brain, a soul, and something to say. Andy Samberg's newest film is Palm Springs, and it checks all of those boxes masterfully.
reviews.author: Tim Brennan

reviews.text: There's a lot going in here that feels larger than a 90-minute film. But even when the parts of the whole don't cohere, Palm Springs is unceasingly warm and pleasant.
reviews.author: Andrew Kendall

reviews.text: Every scene serves a purpose... The ultimate payoff feels earned because of how incredible the chemistry is between the two leads.
reviews.author: Austin Burke

reviews.text: Skittish, existential sci-fi - perfectly timed for quarantine viewing.
reviews.author: Susan Granger

reviews.text: Samberg and Milioti's ironic, wiry performances and chemistry keep it afloat even when the script isn't operating at 100%.
reviews.author: Tim Brayton

reviews.text: Parts of Palm Springs seem like a more adult-language version of a Saturday Night Live sketch that's worn out its welcome ... Huge stretches of Palm Springs drag on for too long. And even the movie's visual effects look cheap and clunky.
reviews.author: Carla Hay

reviews.text: Samberg can be a huge screen presence. In Palm Springs, he and Milioti have amazing chemistry and share the screen effortlessly. Samberg is more restrained than usual, toning down his performance allows Milioti to shine.
reviews.author: Scott Phillips

reviews.text: Along with continual laugh-out-loud gags, there's humour that's very close to the knuckle, finding surprising resonance even as the film celebrates the absurdity of everyday life.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: It's funny, clever, charming, and refreshing -- exactly what I needed it to be.
reviews.author: Marianna Neal

reviews.text: A romantic comedy that uses the concept of a time loop quite intelligently. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Sebastian Zavala Kahn

reviews.text: There were enough twists and updates on the formula to consider Palm Springs a refreshing take. It was cute and enjoyable, but I probably won't turn it on again.
reviews.author: Courtney Lanning

reviews.text: In a year desperate for and largely devoid of fun, it's a welcome romp.
reviews.author: Josh Davis

reviews.text: Watch this before some big-mouthed, dopey movie critic spoils the plot for you!
reviews.author: Bob Grimm

reviews.text: It breaks the -seemingly eternal- cycle of forgettable romantic comedies. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Nestor Bentancor

reviews.text: ...its story about a time loop is eminently relatable to a citizenry stuck in its own monotonous quarantine routine... even more ironic is the fact that PALM SPRINGS is incredibly watchable over and over again.
reviews.author: Jeff York

reviews.text: One of the most exhilarating films of the year, the rare movie with massive buzz out of Sundance that lives up to the hype
reviews.author: Stephen Silver

reviews.text: It really exceeds at what it's trying to do: an inventive new take on Groundhog Day. It has very likable lead performances by Andy Samberg and Cristin Milioti, and it has more on its mind than the run-of-the-mill rom-com.
reviews.author: Claudia Puig

reviews.text: A star is born: Milioti is amazing in this.
reviews.author: Wade Major

reviews.text: Sweet and funny, and surprisingly original for a derivative high-concept movie.
reviews.author: Michael J. Casey

reviews.text: There's still room for intellectual growth for The Lonely Island and the other makers of Palm Springs, but they've made an intriguing leap forward...
reviews.author: Rubén Rosario

reviews.text: It plays into the dystopian fantasy of being able to reinvent yourself in a lawless world, delivering a clever tale about what it takes for someone who's not a part of existence to want to reengage with life.
reviews.author: Matt Fowler

reviews.text: The wacky existential rom-com we need in 2020.
reviews.author: Sarah Marrs

reviews.text: Andy Samberg is a great romantic lead, which I hadn't thought of him before in and he can handle the drama and comedy. It's a new side of Samberg.
reviews.author: Paul McGuire Grimes

reviews.text: It was inventive in the sense that I paused it several times and remarked 'I have no idea where this is heading,' (a good thing). Andy Samberg was near perfect in the lead.
reviews.author: Patrick McDonald

reviews.text: The protagonists of Palm Springs quietly subvert gender roles.
reviews.author: Li Lai

reviews.text: Smart, sharp-witted romantic comedy with two equal leads and a dollop of dark humor.
reviews.author: Brad Keefe

reviews.text: Samberg's goofy charm is perfect for Nyles, but Milioti is just as charming. They create such wonderful chemistry that you can't help but be emotionally invested in their journey.
reviews.author: Micheal Compton

reviews.text: By subverting expectations of familiar rom-com tropes, the film manages to offer something slightly different while remaining wholly comforting.
reviews.author: Emily Alford

reviews.text: More than anything, "Springs" posits that an appreciation for the small wonders that life presents us is the key to happiness and that the trap so many of us fall into is that we take these for granted.
reviews.author: Charles Koplinski

reviews.text: For those looking for a silly and somewhat sappy romantic comedy, it's here. If you want something a bit deeper, you can embrace the themes of destiny, fate and control that are grounded in its Carpe Diem worldview.
reviews.author: Catherine Springer

reviews.text: This is a delight that I'd be all too happy to see again.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: Of all the Groundhog Day riffs, Palm Springs is the first to allow JK Simmons to hunt another man for sport. Finally!
reviews.author: Ryan Syrek

reviews.text: Watching Samberg and Milioti play off each other, as they try to find some sort of common ground, is what makes "Palm Springs" enjoyable.
reviews.author: Matthew Passantino

reviews.text: Imagine a writer entering a room to pitch "Groundhog Day" meets "Wedding Crashers." Most of us would love to see that movie - and now we can with "Palm Springs."
reviews.author: Jason Fraley

reviews.text: I won't tell you how it ends, but I will say that Samberg and Milioti are delightful together.
reviews.author: Max Weiss

reviews.text: If you're going to play in the Ramis/Murray sandbox, you better bring your A game.
reviews.author: Chris McCoy

reviews.text: Palm Springs is a delightfully romantic flight-of-fancy with enough salt to avoiding becoming too saccharine and a story that proves there's room for more than one flavor of the Groundhog Day premise.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: With the help of Samberg, Milioti as Sarah, is able to acknowledge love and still be able to let go. This creates a moment that is full of sweet pathos that lifts this movie beyond a simple rom-com with sci-fi overtones.
reviews.author: Linda and Al Lerner

reviews.text: Samberg and Milioti are each at the top of their game here, making you buy into Nyles and Sarah's trials and tribulations. Siara's script is an actor's dream house.
reviews.author: Dan Buffa

reviews.text: Somewhere between the comically somber Groundhog Day and an outlandishly absurd Andy Samberg vehicle sits Palm Springs...
reviews.author: Josh Larsen

reviews.text: One of the year's best romances.
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: Miliotti and Samberg are so brilliant in their roles, I was mesmerized. The depth of their performances in channeling varying degrees of weariness and struggle is worth the price of admission (or clicking play on Hulu).
reviews.author: Terence Johnson

reviews.text: These two appallingly irresponsible characters ... have a lot to learn. [The movie] wears itself out trying to figure out what some of those things might be.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Overstreet

reviews.text: Funny, charming and insanely re-watchable (fittingly on loop!), this romcom delivers some thoughtful, inventive surprises within the genre and the matrimonial hijinks milieu.
reviews.author: Courtney Howard

reviews.text: Hilarious, offbeat, and delightful.
reviews.author: Bobby LePire

reviews.text: An entertaining dark comedy that's not as funny as it could be, and not as clever as it wishes it was.
reviews.author: Louisa Moore

reviews.text: Couple is stuck in a time loop; sex, drugs, language.
reviews.author: Barbara Shulgasser

reviews.text: Palm Springs is definitely funny, but it's a darker, hazier affair.
reviews.author: Joshua Rivera

reviews.text: An amusing and thoughtful romcom.
reviews.author: Kyle Smith

reviews.text: Palm Springs is a reminder of what the romantic comedy does best: bringing the laughs and teaching us a thing or two about love and life.
reviews.author: Natasha Alvar

reviews.text: [Palm Springs] seamlessly blends romance, comedy, science fiction, and heart-wrenching emotional drama.
reviews.author: Brianna Wellen

reviews.text: And indie rom-com with a lot of heart and more than a few original moments...the love story of our time, wacky courageous and fresh.
reviews.author: Shawn Edwards

reviews.text: ...but its particular approach to the time-loop genre also has the added benefit of being a profoundly moving recreation of what quarantine has felt like for so many of us, especially those quarantined as a couple.
reviews.author: Dominic Griffin

reviews.text: Made up of contradicting bits, of square pegs in round holes, it manages to work because of a clever script and central performances by Andy Samberg and Cristin Milioti that anchor the film when it begins to race beyond its boundaries.
reviews.author: Allyson Johnson

reviews.text: Samberg's performance is pitch perfect and his command of subtlety (something he's not traditionally known for) is impressive... With that said, the movie really belongs to Milioti.
reviews.author: Cristina Iskander

reviews.text: The supporting cast of characters enhances every aspect of the film.
reviews.author: Pamela Powell

reviews.text: Near-perfect, proving to be a moving, hilarious and breathtaking work.
reviews.author: Grant Hermanns

reviews.text: Every element just blends so seamlessly that it creates an airtight, grin-inducing hour and a half of comedy, romance, and time travel that will from now on be our go-to feel-good movie.
reviews.author: Lauren Coates

reviews.text: By not taking itself so seriously, Barbakow and Siara are successful in mining its whimsical possibilities, but it's an exercise frittering away meaningfulness for what, at the end of the day, is merely another quirky romantic comedy.
reviews.author: Nicholas Bell

reviews.text: This is a fresh, funny, and original take on a time-honored trope.
reviews.author: Tim Appelo

reviews.text: Palm Springs will amaze with its ingenuity and intelligence. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ruben Peralta Rigaud

reviews.text: What a dazzling vision of the purgatorial: a desert of vast eternity, strewn with so-so canapés, stumblebum speeches, and worse dancing. Sisyphus had it easy.
reviews.author: Anthony Lane

reviews.text: Director Max Barbakow, marking his debut, and writer Andy Siara craft a wonderfully smart, weird vehicle for Samberg, whose goofy smile and wide-eyed joke delivery continues be a winning combination.
reviews.author: Matthew Dougherty

reviews.text: A thoroughly engaging and ingratiating sci-fi comedy...
reviews.author: David Nusair

reviews.text: Its phoniness feels like painting a patio blue and calling it a pool, and then being dumb enough to jump in.
reviews.author: Matt Pais

reviews.text: Real love doesn't just accept the best parts of a person, but also the many imperfections. Palm Springs is a story for anyone who has been through the ugly side of love and who has emerged all the better for it.
reviews.author: Adriana Gomez-Weston

reviews.text: While it's funny to watch a dorky couple stumble through a repetitive life with IDGAF attitudes, the story wears thin and Nyles and Sarah really learn nothing of value, unlike Bill Murray's character in Groundhog Day, which was brilliantly nuanced.
reviews.author: Kiko Martinez

reviews.text: [A] wonderful take on the time loop trope that manages to feel both self-referential and original...In a world where so many are currently stuck on repeat, the idea that meaning itself can erode through repetition is a timely one.
reviews.author: Allen Adams

reviews.text: It isn't, in the end, about falling in love, finding yourself, or discovering the meaning of life. Its time loop is about living life with what you've got.
reviews.author: Matthew Razak

reviews.text: Encapsulating the refreshingly light feel of a summer movie, Palm Springs constructs an assured reinvention of its tried and true set-up.
reviews.author: Matt Conway

reviews.text: A derivative and desperate-to-be-"dark" comedy.
reviews.author: Rafer Guzman

reviews.text: Watch it; it's fun.
reviews.author: Linda Holmes

reviews.text: Palm Springs proves there's plenty of life left in the time loop subgenre when smart filmmakers and a charming cast are involved.
reviews.author: Shaun Munro

reviews.text: Great chemistry between the leads and a clever premise results in the best romantic comedy of the year, so far. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fico Cangiano

reviews.text: A great balance of comedy, drama, romance, science fiction - there's a lot of genres at play here. One of 2020's better films.
reviews.author: Dan Murrell

reviews.text: While Palm Springs does speak to the undying human hunger for love that all great rom-coms must, the existential premise necessitates darker questions. Even if you've found someone to endure the forces with, is that enough to make life worth it?
reviews.author: Selome Hailu

reviews.text: The film never stops being funny, even when the mood takes a downturn from zany good times to dejection. This is key.
reviews.author: Andy Crump

reviews.text: Zinging between humor and poignance with a lot of charm, it achieves in its most insightful moments what comedy does best: Let us laugh at the world a little, by way of learning something about ourselves.
reviews.author: Alissa Wilkinson

reviews.text: As refreshing as a pool on a hot summer day.
reviews.author: Asher Luberto

reviews.text: Palm Springs is about how reality can feel endless, and how being an adult involves cherishing the truth that a lot of things will never change.
reviews.author: David Sims

reviews.text: Wacky and weird but never obnoxious, the film benefits from endearing performances, plus an ability to venture into surreal territory without bogging down in metaphysical mumbo-jumbo.
reviews.author: Todd Jorgenson

reviews.text: Feels unlike anything else that's been released recently and is a thoroughly entertaining summer movie
reviews.author: Lea Palmieri

reviews.text: Palm Springs endeared me to Samberg and Milioti quite a bit, and that's not nothing. The movie, though, doesn't amount to much.
reviews.author: K. Austin Collins

reviews.text: This feels derivative almost to the point of distraction. And while its try-and-try-again exchanges can be pretty funny, the film feels as if it's laboring to flesh out even the under-90-minute running time.
reviews.author: Brian Lowry

reviews.text: For the most part, it is very funny, occasionally wise and the kind of film that should have no problem standing up to repeat viewing.
reviews.author: Peter Sobczynski

reviews.text: A nice twist to the time loop comedy that has some good gags, but underdeveloped writing leaves the two leads unable to find that all-important connection to click things into place.
reviews.author: Steven Sheehan

reviews.text: "Palm Springs" is a love story for a world where every day's exactly the same, and while you might find that a little eerily on point just now, it's also a comfort.
reviews.author: Ty Burr

reviews.text: Palm Springs is, undoubtedly, one of the best romantic comedies we've seen in years because it breaks down the way we engage with films of the genre.
reviews.author: Sabrina Ramirez

reviews.text: Palm Springs' major upgrade to Groundhog Day is that it takes Andie McDowell's character, gives her a personality, and includes her in the day-repeat antics. In most other ways, the film is a downgrade.
reviews.author: Neal Pollack

reviews.text: "Palm Springs" is worth the trip.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: There are heavy themes in Palm Springs but thanks to Samberg and Milioti, they rarely feel that way. Each is so charming, vulnerable, and hilarious, the story moves like a rocketship fueled by adorable awkwardness.
reviews.author: Germain Lussier

reviews.text: You may think you know where it's going, but Barbakow and screenwriter Andy Siara keep it fresh, developing ideas in a constant state of flux.
reviews.author: Sheila O'Malley

reviews.text: This is a love story about two depressed, anxiety-ridden people whose mental states are constantly deteriorating. But it is also demented, charming, and funny as hell.
reviews.author: Alan Zilberman

reviews.text: Joining the ranks [of time loop films] is a film which finds something not only unique in its handling of the time loop but also profoundly thoughtful and emotionally evocative ...
reviews.author: Douglas Davidson

reviews.text: He's good, she's great, and together they're just a couple trying to navigate life one-day-at-a-time...just like the rest of us.
reviews.author: Tom Santilli

reviews.text: You can see where the story is headed, and you don't mind in the slightest.
reviews.author: Justin Chang

reviews.text: You may have heard a version of this story before, but in this setting it becomes newly fresh, bizarre, and delightfully worthwhile.
reviews.author: Jeva Lange

reviews.text: The paths of this story, these characters, and this relationship constantly surprise.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: A genially mediocre time-killer that feels far more at home on your television set than it did on a big screen.
reviews.author: Sean Burns

reviews.text: Samberg and Milioti make that burgeoning romance feel genuine, even in the midst of such a bizarre situation.
reviews.author: Josh Bell

reviews.text: A winning comedy that combines a goofy sense of humor with genuine heart.
reviews.author: Adam Lubitow

reviews.text: Not only does Palm Springs feel like a level-up for the Lonely Island troupe, but it also seems like a crowdpleaser with an odd mean streak rare enough to be a hit.
reviews.author: Nick Harley

reviews.text: What it has to say about loneliness and finding purpose when our lives are stripped of impact and progression is quite profound and brims with urgency.
reviews.author: Oliver Jones

reviews.text: Both leads' charms go a long way toward papering over certain stumbles in Andy Siara's script, which tends to lean on sitcom setups and the kind of quick-fire banter that seldom exists outside of a certain school of self-aware screenwriting.
reviews.author: Leah Greenblatt

reviews.text: It might just be the perfect time for an inventive comedy about isolation and repetition.
reviews.author: Steve Pond

reviews.text: Its fun take on the traditional romantic comedy makes this one of the must see movies on Hulu. The premise is great while the story is touching. Samberg and Miloti have great chemistry.
reviews.author: Nathaniel Muir

reviews.text: The kind of sophisticated extrapolation of Groundhog Day one would hope for.
reviews.author: Fred Topel

reviews.text: "Palm Springs" isn't entirely original, but it's hard to resist the tweaks and changes to the "Groundhog Day" style. Not to mention Andy Samberg and Cristin Milioti are a perfect match, delivering laughs and charm galore.
reviews.author: Nate Adams

reviews.text: [A] wildly funny, admirably inventive movie...
reviews.author: A.O. Scott

reviews.text: Worry not. Sarah and Nyles are stuck in time, but screenwriter Andy Siara does inventive things with their cosmic staycation.
reviews.author: John Anderson

reviews.text: The movie is so light on its feet that it never feels forced or didactic, even when it asks us to confront piercing truths about love and the elusive meaning of happiness.
reviews.author: Stephanie Zacharek

reviews.text: Few films make me want to watch them again on the spot. "Palm Springs" did.
reviews.author: Randy Myers

reviews.text: Endlessly charming, richly entertaining, and laugh-out-loud funny, it's one of the best romantic comedies in years.
reviews.author: Doug Jamieson

reviews.text: Palm Springs is the most unlikely of life lessons disguised as a comedic time loop with spot performances from Andy Samberg, Cristin Milioti and J.K. Simmons
reviews.author: Carla Renata

reviews.text: Palm Springs is both a look at existential crisis and a riotously funny movie examining relationships
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: An intelligent and consistently funny crowd-pleaser with more than enough chemistry to satisfy hungry rom-com audiences.
reviews.author: Sean O'Connell

reviews.text: Likes to visit comedic chaos, but doesn't want to stay there, showing more interest in the psychological test of the time loop, and how it changes the characters, mixing some existential pressure with goofball humor.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: If you are in search of a romantic comedy that is smart, funny, and (dare I say) original, then you definitely have to watch "Palm Springs."
reviews.author: Jason Guerrasio

reviews.text: Even if it feels like you're reliving "Groundhog Day" while watching "Palm Springs," the rom-com finds its own sunny spin on the material.
reviews.author: Rob Thomas

reviews.text: A near-perfect, sneakily provocative romcom that sets a never better Andy Samberg and Cristin Milioti on a time loop where repetition can kill sex drives and even the will to live, but still leaves you laughing gratefully at the resilience of love.
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: Though made before our collective nightmare, Palm Springs is the movie for our hellish moment and one of the best movies of this absolutely bizarre year.
reviews.author: Sean Mulvihill

reviews.text: It's easy to see why Hulu and Neon dropped all that cash on it. This is the stuff of streams.
reviews.author: Johnny Oleksinski

reviews.text: Silly, stylish, sneaky profound, and damned near perfect.
reviews.author: Vincent Mancini

reviews.text: "Palm Springs" is more than just an utterly delightful romantic comedy, it's one of the smartest and most creative films of the year. I smiled from ear to ear for 90 minutes.
reviews.author: Joey Magidson

reviews.text: Along with a sharp sense of humor and compelling performances, Palm Springs delivers an absolutely charming rom-com with a fun sci-fi twist.
reviews.author: Molly Freeman

reviews.text: Cheating girlfriends, ludicrous wedding guests and even J.K. Simmons coked out of his mind is not enough to salvage things.
reviews.author: Martin Carr

reviews.text: The mix of quirkiness and honest heart and emotion makes it one of Samberg's better endeavors.
reviews.author: Edward Douglas

reviews.text: While the romantic comedy is not fully back, despite think pieces assuring us that it is, Palm Springs energetically reminds us, yet again, that it's never really going away.
reviews.author: Benjamin Lee

reviews.text: Ultimately, the measure of "Palm Springs" isn't the cleverness or resonance of its premise but rather how creatively it fulfills that premise.
reviews.author: Mick LaSalle

reviews.text: "Palm Springs" belongs to Milioti, in a breakout performance... this feels like the first leading film role for Milioti that allows her to show new shades of her range. She's darker, funnier, wackier than she's been before, but still grounded.
reviews.author: Katie Walsh

reviews.text: As Groundhog Day's various imitators have taught us, there's a certain amount of pleasure in repetition.
reviews.author: Matt Singer

reviews.text: While not new, the idea of a time loop can be fun. I mean, I just think Groundhogs Day as a point of reference.Andy and Cristin are a fun duo with great chemistry. This film was a good time and definitely worth the watch.
reviews.author: Derek Sante

reviews.text: One of its immediate pleasures comes in how dexterously it skims past many of the obligatory beats in order to get to less-explored territory.
reviews.author: Alison Willmore

reviews.text: A raunchy sci-fi rom-com that utilizes the time loop device brilliantly to tell a smart, character-driven tale, resulting in one of my favorite comedies of 2020 thus far.
reviews.author: Rendy Jones

reviews.text: You can't reinvent the wheel, but you can make it roll in a quirky way. That's what Barbakow does with "Palm Springs."
reviews.author: Bill Goodykoontz

reviews.text: Here's a terrific film that manages to subvert a particular sub-genre of film, and deliver on being an ambitious romantic comedy.
reviews.author: Aaron Neuwirth

reviews.text: [It's] a romantic comedy out of damnation more than anything else, which, while thematically fitting, allows its characters to function as both people and meta devices.
reviews.author: Matt Cipolla

reviews.text: Andy Samberg in his most engaging screen performance yet in Max Barbakow's funny, smart, and twisted movie that despite sounding like Groundhog Day at a Wedding turns out to be the most blissfully original comedy of 2020.
reviews.author: Pete Hammond

reviews.text: Palm Springs is laugh-out-loud funny and so gosh-darn endearing. It is respectful of its audience and profoundly offers something that feels real.
reviews.author: Caitlin Kennedy

reviews.text: Palm Springs is hilarious, affecting and weird, and features two brilliant performances from Andy Samberg and Cristin Milioti. Don't read any more until you've seen the movie.
reviews.author: Ian Sandwell

reviews.text: The film smuggles some surprisingly bleak existential questioning inside a brightly comedic vehicle.
reviews.author: Chris Barsanti

reviews.text: Going into it blind is a great idea. Just go see it!
reviews.author: Avaryl Halley

reviews.text: My jaw was hurting I was laughing so much
reviews.author: Andrew Galdi

reviews.text: Emerges as the rarest of rare rom-coms: A rom-com with something meaningful to say that never ceases to engage or entertain.
reviews.author: Mel Valentin

reviews.text: Samberg and Milioti are great together.
reviews.author: Mike Ryan

reviews.text: Barbakow paces the story, particularly the backward leapfrog of the resetting timer, with precision. But he also leaves room for his leads room to let the jokes and their personalities come out.
reviews.author: Sean P. Means

reviews.text: The scenes between Milioti and Samberg were very funny, refreshing and well-executed.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: It's highly entertaining, it is an often hilarious comedy, and it's also got real purpose and heart at its core.
reviews.author: Perri Nemiroff

reviews.text: The film, directed by Max Barbakow and written by Andy Siara, pretty quickly reveals its premise, but there's still a pleasure in experiencing how they let the cat out of the bag.
reviews.author: A.A. Dowd

reviews.text: You have to do the work in order to use Kate Bush properly, and I'm glad to say that Palm Springs earns the right with flying colors.
reviews.author: Nick Johnston

reviews.text: The charming Palm Springs puts a different spin on the romantic comedy genre in a way that will certainly feel familiar to viewers.
reviews.author: Danielle Solzman

reviews.text: Palm Springs is a surprisingly heartfelt rom-com that manages to eke out assured performances from both Andy Samberg and Christin Milioti.
reviews.author: Clint Worthington

reviews.text: Palm Springs doesn't get bogged down by extemporaneous storylines and marginal characters, traits that often plague small comedies like this.
reviews.author: Jake Kring-Schreifels

reviews.text: There's a massive, Groundhog Day-evoking twist that instantly transports this from cute rom-com to high-concept deconstruction of a rom-com that illuminates our need for connection-of course, filtered through the wily charms of Lonely Island.
reviews.author: Kevin Fallon

reviews.text: A wildly entertaining entry in a genre that is on life support lately, the romantic comedy.
reviews.author: Brian Tallerico

reviews.text: Samberg possesses a bleak brand of sarcastic optimism that gives Palm Springs plenty of laughs laced with a tinge of unease.
reviews.author: Ian Thomas Malone

reviews.text: At its core it's actually quite sweet and funny
reviews.author: Rachel Wagner

reviews.text: A hilarious comedy, heartbreaking drama, and genuinely moving love story that dares to say that maybe life is a little better with a companion by your side.
reviews.author: Adam Chitwood

reviews.text: It really is impressive to see a comedy with this much unassuming, laid-back charm also come packaged with a deep affection for both its characters and its audience.
reviews.author: Jon Negroni

reviews.text: Palm Springs knows this dread. It lives in it. It invites you to laugh about it, and maybe shed a few tears over it, and when it's all done, maybe you'll finally have an answer to the question of what love could possibly be worth at the edge of the void.
reviews.author: Angie Han

reviews.text: Despite retreading the familiar time-loop trope, the film is silly but incredibly entertaining - one of the funniest movies you will likely see this year.
reviews.author: Jordan Ruimy

reviews.text: Andy Samberg, Christin Milioti, and director Max Barbakow make the time loop comedy new again (and again, and again).
reviews.author: Karl Delossantos

reviews.text: "Palm Springs" is to time-loop movies as "Zombieland" was to the undead genre: It's an irreverent take on a form where earlier iterations were obliged to take themselves seriously.
reviews.author: Peter Debruge

reviews.text: The story may be familiar... But the execution here feels fresh and playful, with a new energy coming from Samberg and Milioti's go-for-broke performances, and some new iterations on the formula.
reviews.author: Tasha Robinson

reviews.text: The movie always seems on the brink of biting off more than a super energetic 90-minute comedy can chew, and the sheer momentum of the storytelling doesn't give the story time to slow down.
reviews.author: David Ehrlich

reviews.text: The two incredibly likeable leads and the anarchic edge that comes with its Lonely Island affiliation makes Palm Springs a legit crowdpleaser and an A plus date movie.
reviews.author: Chris Bumbray

reviews.text: Max Barbakow's raunchy rom-com, Palm Springs, adds meaning to the seeming meaninglessness of life, with infectious fun and introspective pleasure to boot.
reviews.author: Robert Daniels

reviews.text: Pointlessness, isolation and the guarantee that no one will ever understand your plight may not sound like the makings of a laugh-filled heartwarmer, but in the hands of Barbakow and screenwriter Andy Siara, it is.
reviews.author: John DeFore

synopsis: Stuck in a time loop, two wedding guests develop a budding romance while living the same day over and over again.
